chunks: Do not deny good counsel to yourself, good behaviour to the army, succour to the subjects and strength to the religion of Allāh. Strive in the way of Allāh as is obligatory on you, because Allāh the Glorified, desires us and you to be thankful to Him as best as we can and that we should help Him to the best of our power. And there is no power save with Allāh, the All-high, the All-glorious.
ai.seo_question: What are the four things one should not withhold according to this passage from Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this exhortation to tax collectors, Imam Ali (AS) defines the ideal administrative conduct as selfless generosity, urging officials to expend their own resources, military strength, and support for the populace in the service of God. This reflects the Shia principle of *ihsan* (excellence) in governance, where leaders are expected to go beyond mere duty, recognizing that their efforts are a form of gratitude (*shukr*) for divine empowerment. The closing phrase 'La quwwata illa billah' underscores that all administrative efficacy ultimately derives from God's will.
